# dsh-gitbash
**English** | 简体中文

A Windows terminal bridge for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. It replaces the
model-facing `pwsh` tool w

ith a real `bash` tool, with selectable **Git for
Windows** and **MSYS2** profiles, while keeping th

e official terminal-tool
behaviour: working directory, background jobs, timeout promotion, permissio

n
escalation, terminal cards, PTC and `meta.cwd`.

This is the complete user manual and reference. It covers installation, daily
usage, the security mo
del, settings, troubleshooting and development.

> **Minimum DSH: 0.2.2.** Windows 10/11 only. The replacement applies to **new
> sessions**; existin
g sessions keep the tools they were created with.
## What you get

- **One `bash`, no `pwsh`** in the model tool catalogue: `tools.restrict` hides
`pwsh`, the `tool:pw

sh` prompt section is shadowed, and `tool:bash` is added.
The replacement applies to new sessions; e

xisting ones are not retrofitted.
- **Two shell families, one selector**: Git for Windows (default p

riority) or
MSYS2 (`UCRT64`, `MINGW64`, `CLANG64`, `CLANGARM64`, `MINGW32`, `MSYS`).
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements
| Item | Requirement |

| DSH | `>= 0.2.2` (tested on desktop runtime `0.2.2-rc.1`) |
| Windows | Windows 10/11, x64; MSYS2

arm64 environments are also supported |
| bash provider | Git for Windows and/or MSYS2 |
| Node.js |

`>= 24.9`, development/build only (the DSH 0.2.2 floor) |
| Optional | Cygwin, best-effort and not

evelopment/build only (the DSH 0.2.2 floor) |
| Optional | Cygwin, best-effort and not recommended |

- Git Bash and MSYS2 both use the MSYS2 runtime. That runtime cannot start
inside DSH's Windows ACL

sandbox; this is an OS constraint, not a plugin bug
(evidence in docs/DESIGN.md).
- WSL's `bash.exe`

is intentionally excluded. WSL is not Git Bash and does not
fit this profile/environment model.
## Security model (read this first)

The MSYS2 runtime cannot start under DSH's Windows ACL sandbox: restricted
tokens break its named sh

ared memory, signal pipe and `BaseNamedObjects`. Adding
the user SID defeats write confinement; lowe

ring to Low integrity breaks
`BaseNamedObjects` again. There is no configuration in which Git Bash b

oth runs
and stays inside that sandbox.
The plugin therefore makes the trade-off **explicit**:
| Session permission | `compat: auto` (default) | `compat: strict` |

| `danger-full-access` | bash runs normally | bash runs normally |
| `workspace-write` | bash runs *

*outside the file sandbox**, result carries `[compat: ...]` | **refused** |
| `read-only` | **refuse

andbox**, result carries `[compat: ...]` | **refused** |
| `read-only` | **refused** | **refused** |

- **File tools remain sandboxed** by DSH. Only the bash process is unconfined.
- Under `workspace-wr

ite` + `auto`, bash can write outside the workspace. Treat
paths outside the workspace as read-only

unless the user explicitly asks
otherwise.
- The plugin never silently widens permissions. The warni

ng is always in the
settings row, the tool description and the system prompt; every unconfined
resul

t also carries the `[compat: ...]` note.
- `read-only` deliberately refuses rather than breaking the

read-only promise.
- `strict` is for security-sensitive users: bash is available only under
`danger

-full-access`.
- A blocked call can be retried with `sandbox_permissions` plus a one-sentence
`justi

fication`; DSH asks the user for approval, and the wider mode applies to
that call only.
## Compatibility and upgrades

- Minimum DSH: **0.2.2**. The plugin uses structural projections of official
services (`ctx.subproce

ss`, `ctx.jobs`, `ctx.sandboxPolicy`, `ctx.shellEnv`,
`ctx.workingDirectory`, `ctx.approval`, `ctx.c

onfigForms`, etc.) and does not
import private DSH packages.
- Replacement needs `ctx.subprocess.spa

wn` **and** `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve`:
bash is spawned outside DSH's confinement, so the policy se

rvice is the only
source of the session mode. If either is missing, the plugin keeps the
preset's `p

wsh` and the settings row shows the missing capability.
- `agent/created`, `tools.restrict`, `tool:b

ash` / `tool:pwsh` section names,
result markers and `meta.cwd` are the critical integration points.

A wrong
event name would be a silent no-op, so the test suite asserts the strings.
- After upgradin

g DSH:
1. `pnpm compatcheck`
2. `pnpm test`
3. rebuild (`pnpm build`) if `src/` changed; the committ

ed `lib/` must match
`src/`
4. restart DSH and hard-refresh the Web UI
- Non-Windows does not regist

er any behaviour: `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.platforms: ["win32"]` (DSH 0.2.2 Host admissio

n) and
`cordis.patch.yml` disables the entry when `process.platform !== 'win32'`.

**Verified on 2026-11-06:** DSH `0.2.2-rc.1`, Git for Windows 2.56 and MSYS2
5.3.20 (UCRT64); direct

bash, promoted results, background jobs, subagents,
SIGTERM normalization, relative workdir, strict

refusal and the real settings
row (MSYS2 switch through the UI) were exercised — 31/31 scenario che

cks and
15/15 UI checks on a clean browser load. The 0.2.5 audit added a 13/13 manual
path flow (MSY

S2 → Git) through the real UI. The 0.2.6 audit added read-only
refusal, approval allow/deny, workspa

ce-write escalation labeling, a 108 KB
tail/spill result, a live `job_kill`, `/tmp` workdir, end-to-

end clearing of a
hostile `BASH_ENV`/exported function, and a clean final settings row. Raw
events:

f a
hostile `BASH_ENV`/exported function, and a clean final settings row. Raw
events: docs/SMOKE.md.
## Limitations and non-goals

- **One-shot bash**: every call is `bash -c`, not a persistent shell/PTY. The
`minimal` preset's per

sistent shell is not preserved.
- **Windows sandbox incompatibility**: bash cannot run confined; see

Security model. There is no safe toggle
that makes MSYS2 run inside the ACL sandbox.
- **WSL exclud

ed**; Cygwin is best-effort and experimental.
- **Existing sessions are not migrated**; settings app

ly to new agents.
- **Background jobs have no timeout**; stop them explicitly.
- **Output is tail-tr

uncated**; use the spill file for full output.
- **The replacement is per-agent**: a child inherits

the parent's layer, but a
child created before the plugin was active will not be retrofitted.
